Subject: KMS gateway + proxy for on-prem BYOK: attenuation & rotation runbook

Team —

Following the on-site kickoff with Acme last week, I sketched a proposal for a small-footprint KMS gateway/proxy that sits in the customer VPC and mediates HSM-backed key operations for Redwood Private deployments. The high-level goals and constraints:

- Goals:
  - Allow Acme to maintain their BYOK HSM while letting Redwood services perform tokenized operations (sign/encrypt) with minimal egress.
  - Provide predictable rotation windows with automated, reversible rollouts (canary -> full) so we don't cause mass TTL expiry during rotations.
  - Produce an operable runbook for NOC/CS to execute cutovers and emergency rollback.
- Constraints:
  - No new persistent inbound egress ports from customer network; all comms must be outbound and mutually authenticated (mTLS + attestation).
  - Operator separation: customer operators must not have host-level access to Redwood control plane keys; split custody for ceremony.
  - Rotation windows must tolerate 60s median token latency spikes and preserve streaming KV cache coherency.

Attached: kms-proxy-sequence.pdf — diagram + sequence flows.

Asks: can you review for operational gaps and list any acceptance tests we should add to the cutover checklist? I want to share a 1.0 runbook with Acme by EOD Thursday (2025-07-17).

Notes: I'll propose an "attenuated rotation" approach in the runbook: roll small sets of pods through a short overlap window so old tokens continue to be honored for X minutes while new keys propagate. See section 3 in the diagram.

Rafael
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Rafael — quick pass from an ops perspective. This looks promising; a few concrete operational tweaks: 

1) Attestation and nonce flow: add an optional CA-signed attestation token exchange during initial connector bootstrap. That addresses Acme's security team ask for measurable proof of identity without opening outbound port exceptions.

2) Rotation TTLs and cache overlap: be explicit about three windows in the runbook — generate, propagate, expire. For streaming workloads we want: generate window (1m), propagation grace (5m), expire window (10m). The exact numbers are workload-dependent but giving defaults is useful.

3) Operator separation / SRE drills: add a pre-cutover simulated rollback test step where we forcibly scale a canary downstream and validate signature fallbacks. Include acceptance criteria (no >0.5% error rate, <200ms p90 latency impact).

4) Monitoring hooks: emit a "key-proxy-rotation" event with old/new key IDs, rotation-phase, and correlation-id to our observability sink. This should be critical (not debug) so on-call sees it.

I've attached a small patch with suggested wording and an example audit log entry: rotation-playbook-diff.patch.

On the network side: agree with outbound-only, but call out that some customers will want a private endpoints/backhauls option (VPC peering or dedicated transit) — document both patterns.

Tessa
Principal Engineer, Ops

Dylan / Rafael — thanks for the clear summary and artifacts. Short answers: 

1) Attestation tokens: yes. Our appliance supports an X.509-based attestation token (RFC style) and can emit a signed blob compatible with mTLS client auth. Typical recommended TTL is 10 minutes for bootstrap tokens; for longer-running connectors we recommend short-lived session tokens minted by the appliance after successful attestation.

2) Revocation proofs: we can emit a revocation proof object (JSON blob) on key rollback. We can sign the blob with the HSM signing key. Recommend you persist these blobs in the audit bundle attached to the rotation event.

Implementation caveats:
- Network: outbound-only is fine but the appliance must be allowed to reach your control-plane egress endpoints (we suggest CIDR allowlist per your docs).
- Time sync: appliance clocks must be within 5s of NTP to validate token TTLs reliably.

We'll create a short integration note for your team and a sample attestation JWT + verification snippet; expect a follow-up within 48 hours.

Regards,
SecureVault Support
support@securevault.io
